/-!
# Maximal run lengths in the second MSB of Tribonacci numbers $T(n)$

The Tribonacci numbers $T_n$ (A000073).
$T_0=0, T_1=0, T_2=1$, and $T_n = T_{n-1} + T_{n-2} + T_{n-3}$ for $n \ge 3$.

Second most significant bit of the tribonacci number A000073(n).
This is formalized by extracting the bit at position $\lfloor \log_2 T_n \rfloor - 1$.

*References:*
- [A271591](https://oeis.org/A271591)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
- [A000073](https://oeis.org/A000073)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA271591


open Nat

/--
The Tribonacci numbers $T_n$ (A000073).
$T_0=0, T_1=0, T_2=1$, and $T_n = T_{n-1} + T_{n-2} + T_{n-3}$ for $n \ge 3$.
-/
def tribonacci (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  match n with
  | 0 => 0
  | 1 => 0
  | 2 => 1
  | n + 3 => (tribonacci (n + 2)) + (tribonacci (n + 1)) + (tribonacci n)

/--
Second most significant bit of the tribonacci number A000073(n).
This is formalized by extracting the bit at position $\lfloor \log_2 T_n \rfloor - 1$.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let T := tribonacci n
  -- The index of the MSB is T.log2. The index of the second MSB is T.log2 - 1.
  if T ≤ 1 then
    0
  else
    let j_smsb : ℕ := T.log2 - 1
    if T.testBit j_smsb then 1 else 0

def IsMaximalRun (v : ℕ) (n L : ℕ) : Prop :=
  n ≥ 2 ∧ L ≥ 1 ∧
  -- The run consists of L consecutive $v$'s starting at n
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < L → a (n + i) = v) ∧
  -- The run is not followed by $v$
  (a (n + L) ≠ v) ∧
  -- The run is not preceded by $v$
  (a (n - 1) ≠ v)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 0 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_6 : a 6 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_7 : a 7 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_8 : a 8 = 1 := by rfl


/--
It is conjectured that after the first two 0's, the number of consecutive 0's is only 4 or 5, and the number of consecutive 1's is only 3 or 4 (tested up to $n = 10^4$).

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/271591.wip.lean#L497"]
theorem maximal_run_lengths : (∀ n L, IsMaximalRun 0 n L → (L = 4 ∨ L = 5)) ∧
    (∀ n L, IsMaximalRun 1 n L → (L = 3 ∨ L = 4)) := by
    sorry

end OeisA271591

reformulations.difference: OEIS starts the sequence at n = 4 and explicitly excepts its initial two zeros. Lean extends a to smaller indices with zeros and handles the exception implicitly: IsMaximalRun requires a different predecessor, without a special case for the first OEIS index.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The computed values are a(0) = ... = a(5) = 0 and a(6) = 1. Consequently every IsMaximalRun starts at n ≥ 6. Define an ordinary maximal run on the OEIS domain n ≥ 4, allowing no predecessor when n = 4. In the scratch file, run_iff_oeis_noninitial proves that IsMaximalRun is exactly this ordinary run predicate together with n ≠ 4, and initial_run_iff proves that the sole omitted run is (value, start, length) = (0, 4, 2). Review.statement_equiv proves the biconditional between the file's statement and the formulation explicitly allowing that exceptional initial zero run. Its only axioms are propext and Quot.sound; it does not use maximal_run_lengths or any sorry-backed result.

review.notes: Checked all three definitions, all five test lemmas, and the main theorem. The Tribonacci recurrence and second-bit extraction agree with the sources. Scratch proofs verify nonvacuous runs (value, start, length) = (1,6,3), (0,9,4), (1,13,4), and (0,17,5), as well as the zero-length and small-index boundaries. An efficient implementation of the same recurrence matched all 9,997 OEIS table entries from indices 4 through 10,000; all completed noninitial runs in that sample satisfy the stated bounds. The research solved status agrees with OEIS's May 28, 2026 proof announcement and the published proof accompanying the cited paper. Direct OEIS entry pages were blocked, so their official data mirror was used. Experiments and the equivalence proof are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the reviewed file was not modified.
